vjimc-2016-cat2-01.prompt:
Let $a,b$ and $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a+b+c=1$. Show that
$$\left(\frac1a+\frac1{bc}\right)\left(\frac1b+\frac1{ca}\right)\left(\frac1c+\frac1{ab}\right)\ge1728 .$$
vjimc-2016-cat2-01.answer: $\frac1a+\frac1{bc}=\frac{(a+b)(a+c)}{abc}$, so the product is $\frac{[(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)]^2}{(abc)^3}\ge\frac{64}{abc}\ge64\cdot27=1728$. Equality holds at $a=b=c=\frac13$.

vjimc-2016-cat2-02.prompt: Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal P(X)$ be the set of all subsets of $X$. Let $\mu\colon\mathcal P(X)\to\mathcal P(X)$ be a map with the property that $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)\cup\mu(B)$ whenever $A$ and $B$ are disjoint subsets of $X$. Prove that there exists a set $F\subset X$ such that $\mu(F)=F$.
vjimc-2016-cat2-02.answer: $\mu$ is monotone. Then $F=\bigcap\{A:\mu(A)\subset A\}$ is a fixed point (Knaster–Tarski).

vjimc-2016-cat2-03.prompt:
For $n\ge3$ find the eigenvalues (with their multiplicities) of the $n\times n$ matrix
$$\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&2&0&1&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\1&0&2&0&1&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&1&0&2&0&1&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&0&1&0&2&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&0&0&1&0&2&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&&\vdots&\vdots\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\0&0&0&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&2&0\\0&0&0&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&1\end{bmatrix}.$$
vjimc-2016-cat2-03.answer: $4\cos^2\frac{k\pi}{n+1}$ for $k=1,\dots,n$. For $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ these are distinct and each has multiplicity $2$; for odd $n$ there is in addition the simple eigenvalue $0$ (from $k=\frac{n+1}2$). The matrix is $B^2$ with $B$ the path adjacency matrix.

vjimc-2016-cat2-04.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable function satisfying
$$f(x)=\int_{x-1}^xf(t)\,dt$$
for all $x\ge1$. Show that $f$ has bounded variation on $[1,\infty)$, i.e.
$$\int_1^\infty|f'(x)|\,dx<\infty .$$
vjimc-2016-cat2-04.answer: For $x\ge1$, $g=f'$ satisfies $g(x)=\int_{x-1}^xg$ and $\int_{x-1}^x(t-x+1)g(t)\,dt=0$. Hence $|g(x)|\le\frac12\max_{[x-1,x]}|g|$, the maxima of $|f'|$ on $[n,n+1]$ decay geometrically, and $\int_1^\infty|f'|<\infty$.
